# StruTrix Studio

> StruTrix Studio is professional Windows software for the structural analysis and steel design of three-dimensional frames, made by RamisoftSolutions for practising engineers on real projects. The program is free, with no limit on model size, no time limit, no watermark and no account required.

## What it does

- Three-dimensional frames of any size: buildings, industrial structures, pipe racks, towers, trusses and transmission poles, drawn member by member or generated.
- First-order analysis, and the AISC 360-22 direct analysis method (second order, P-Delta and P-delta) for every load combination.
- An independent equilibrium audit of every result.
- AISC 360-22 steel design by LRFD and ASD for the sections of the AISC Shapes Database v16.0, every check with its clause, and Optimise, which chooses the lightest section of each group that passes.
- Joint, member, area and thermal loads and self-weight; the ASCE 7-22 load combination generator; line loading by the NESC, ASCE MOP 74 and MOP 113.
- The calculation report.
- Staged construction analysis (Pro): an addition to an existing structure, or a structure built in any number of stages, analysed as it is built. Each stage's loads are carried by the structure standing then, and new members are fitted to where the structure stands. A conventional analysis of the structure built at once lets new members share loads the existing ones carried before they were there, which understates the forces in the existing members and misplaces the load distribution.
- Seismic design of steel systems by ANSI/AISC 341-22 (Pro), with ASCE 7-22's equivalent lateral force, story drift and stability, the capacity-limited analyses of braced frames, the member side of ANSI/AISC 358-22 prequalified moment connections, and the required strengths of column bases, splices and connections.
- The structure link (Pro): FoundaTrix Studio and PileTrix Studio read a saved structure's support reactions from the same cloud job as their loads.

## How its results are checked

- Steel member strengths: 46 strengths printed in the AISC Design Examples (tension, compression, flexure, shear, torsion and combined forces, by LRFD and ASD) reproduced within 1.35%, 43 of them within 1%.
- Second-order analysis: the AISC 360-22 Commentary's benchmark problems (Figures C-C2.2 and C-C2.3) reproduced within 0.37%; the Commentary asks for agreement within 3% in moment and 5% in deflection.
- Beam-column closed forms reproduced within 0.00001%.
- Every design check names its clause, every line of a member's working is evaluated again from its own inputs, and every combination's equilibrium is audited by a separate calculation. More than 1,700 automated tests repeat these with every build.
- Every comparison is published number by number at https://www.strutrix.com/verification/. They are RamisoftSolutions' own comparisons; AISC and ASCE have not reviewed or endorsed the program.

## Where it stands for professional steel design

- Design-code checks: AISC 360-22 by LRFD and ASD, each citing its clause; ANSI/AISC 341-22 seismic design and ASCE/SEI 48-19 tapered tubes (Pro).
- Load combinations: generated by the ASCE 7-22 combination generator, for strength, allowable stress and service, with notional loads.
- Calculation reports: a typeset PDF report (basis, model, loads, combinations, equilibrium, reactions and every member's checks clause by clause), and a member detail that works every check equation by equation with its clause. Both free, with no watermark.
- BIM exchange: export to IFC 4.3 and to Revit as native structural columns and framing (Pro).
- Documentation: a built-in User's Manual in seventeen sections, stating every method, assumption and limit, with pictured tutorials.
- Capacity: no limit on model size; developed and timed on a building of about 10,000 members.
- Connection design: not in the released program. It designs members; a seismic design works the member side of ANSI/AISC 358-22 prequalified moment connections and reports the connections' required strengths. Plate, bolt and weld design is in development (see Coming soon).
- Floor and metal deck design: not in the released program. Composite metal deck floors and their diaphragms are in development (see Coming soon).
- Design codes: United States standards. Eurocode, AS/NZS and other national steel codes are not offered.
- Record of use: a new program, in the Microsoft Store since November 1, 2026. Its frame analysis engine and steel checks also ship in FoundaTrix Studio.

## Free, with no limits

- The free program sets no limit on joints, members, supports, load cases or combinations: a model is as large as the computer can hold. It is developed and timed on a building of about 10,000 members.
- No time limit, no watermark, no advertising and no telemetry. No account is needed, and it works offline.
- It is not a student, educational or evaluation edition: it is the same professional program in every plan, and nothing restricts commercial use.
- A free account adds cloud jobs shared with FoundaTrix Studio and PileTrix Studio, version history, an AI assistant connector, and a free trial of every Pro feature.
- Pro features include staged construction analysis, seismic design by AISC 341-22, tapered tubes to ASCE/SEI 48-19 with the pole and H-frame generators, IFC 4.3 and Revit export, the firm's name and logo on the report, and the structure link. Pro pricing has not been announced.

## Coming soon

These are not available yet, and what each will do may change before it ships.

- Connection design (Pro, in development): a steel frame's connections designed down to every plate, bolt and weld by AISC 360-22 Chapter J, from a library of simple shear and moment connections assigned to member ends and fitted to the true member sections, with the prequalified moment connections of ANSI/AISC 358-22 (reduced beam section, bolted end plates, bolted flange plate, and welded unreinforced flange-welded web) and a 3D connection editor. Today the program designs members, and a seismic design reports the connections' required strengths.
- Composite metal deck design (Pro, in development): floors drawn on plan at a level, with openings, each spanning one way and carrying its own weight, superimposed dead load and live load to the beams under it; their deck designed with the frame along strips between the beams by ANSI/SDI SD-2022 and AISI S100-24, as a form under the wet concrete (Appendix 2) and as a composite deck-slab in service (Section F: flexure, one-way shear, live load deflection, temperature and shrinkage reinforcement), by LRFD or ASD; form deck and bare roof deck too; and each floor designed as a diaphragm by AISI S310-23 and ASCE 7-22 Section 12.10, with its chords and collectors.
- Also on the way: multi-storey buildings modelled from typical floors, and the seismic assessment of steel buildings by pushover to ASCE 41-23.

## The family

StruTrix Studio is one of three programs from RamisoftSolutions, with one account for all of them: FoundaTrix Studio for rigid foundations (https://www.foundatrix.com) and PileTrix Studio for piles (https://www.piletrix.com).
